# NextGen Tabletops

A fun and engaging platform dedicated to board games and card games designed for children and teenagers. The brand revolves around play, discovery, and age-appropriate entertainment, offering a curated selection of games that spark creativity, strategy, and social interaction among young audiences.

# Curated tabletop fun for the next generation.


NextGen Tabletops exists to make board games and card games easier to discover, easier to explain, and more exciting for young players. The platform focuses on age-appropriate fun, social connection, and the joy of learning through play.

















## What guides every recommendation.


We believe the best games create moments of shared joy and discovery. Every game in our curated collection is chosen to support age-appropriate growth, spark laughter around the table, and help parents feel confident in their choices for their children and teenagers.









### Age-appropriate excitement


Games should challenge young players without creating frustration. We match every title to developmental stages so kids and teens feel capable, curious, and eager to play again.









### Social connection


Great tabletop play brings kids, teens, friends, and families into shared moments. Our games encourage teamwork, storytelling, and healthy competition that strengthens real-world bonds.









### Clear discovery


Parents should understand why a game fits before committing time to it. We provide straightforward explanations, age guides, and skill focuses so you can choose with confidence.










## Built for playful discovery without overwhelm.







### Less clutter, more confidence.


We handpick every game to cut through the noise, so parents can trust each recommendation and kids can jump straight into fun without decision fatigue.







### Recommendations shaped around real family situations.


We consider age, group size, and play style — not just popularity — because every game night looks different, and every family deserves a perfect fit.







### A cheerful space where strategy, creativity, and quick fun all belong.


From brain-teasing puzzles to laugh-out-loud party games, our collection celebrates every kind of play — because the best game is the one that brings everyone to the table.











## Let’s make game night easier to choose.


Share the age range, group size, and preferred play style, and NextGen Tabletops can point you in the right direction.








### Ready to find the perfect game?


Our curated collection of board games and card games is waiting for your family. Let us help you discover your next favorite.

Contact NextGen Tabletops












Bringing families together, one game at a time. We curate tabletops that spark imagination and create lasting memories.

# Who are we?






##

###

## Ethan Vance

"Games aren't just about winning or losing; they are about the stories we build together while playing." - Ethan Vance

Born and raised in Australia, Ethan's love affair with gaming began in his childhood, where hours spent around a table sparked a lifetime of imagination. Years later, as a father, that passion found a new purpose. Ethan began inventing custom games for his own children, turning rainy afternoons and family nights into wild, creative adventures.

Watching his kids engage, laugh, and learn, Ethan completely fell in love with the world of modern board and card games designed for children and teens. He saw firsthand how the right game could pull kids away from screens, spark strategy, and build lasting family connections.

Driven by this inspiration, Ethan founded [Insert Company Name]-a dedicated shop and publishing house. Our mission is simple: to bring that same kitchen-table magic to families all over the world, one unforgettable game at a time.






##

###

## Emily Taylor

"If a game doesn't make you laugh, argue passionately, or high-five a rival, we haven't done our job."

Born and raised in Australia, Ethan's love affair with gaming began in his childhood, where hours spent around a table sparked a lifetime of imagination. Years later, as a father, that passion found a new purpose. Ethan began inventing custom games for his own children, turning rainy afternoons and family nights into wild, creative adventures.

Watching his kids engage, laugh, and learn, Ethan completely fell in love with the world of modern board and card games designed for children and teens. He saw firsthand how the right game could pull kids away from screens, spark strategy, and build lasting family connections.

Driven by this inspiration, Ethan founded [Insert Company Name]-a dedicated shop and publishing house. Our mission is simple: to bring that same kitchen-table magic to families all over the world, one unforgettable game at a time.

# A simpler way to pick the next game night favorite.


Use age, play time, group size, and preferred style of fun to make confident tabletop choices for children and teenagers. Our curated collection of board games online and card games helps you find the perfect fit for every young player.




Age fit



Game length



Player count



Play style










## How to Choose the Right Game


Finding the perfect board games and card games for children and teenagers doesn't have to be a puzzle. Follow our simple four-step guide to match every game night to your group's unique energy.




1




### Start with attention span


Match game length to the group's energy and focus. A quick 15-minute round keeps younger players engaged, while teens may enjoy deeper 45-minute adventures.



2




### Choose the social mood


Decide whether the table needs teamwork, competition, creativity, or laughter. Cooperative quests build bonds, while party games spark hilarious memories.



3




### Check teach time


Younger groups usually do best when rules can be explained quickly. Look for games with clear, visual rulebooks that get everyone playing in under 10 minutes.



4




### Plan for replay


Look for games that stay interesting after the first few rounds. Variable setups, hidden roles, or expandable content keep the fun fresh every time you open the box.










## Match the game to the moment.


Every play session has its own rhythm. Find the perfect fit for your family's next game night, travel day, or creative afternoon.











### Quick Play


Best for school nights, travel, and short bursts of laughter. These games pack big fun into small time windows, perfect for busy families on the go.


- After-school wind-down

- Road trip & travel fun

- Playdate icebreakers













### Creative Play


Best for storytelling, drawing, imagination, and collaborative silliness. Unleash young minds with games that turn every player into a creator.


- Rainy day adventures

- Family storytelling nights

- Classroom creativity breaks













### Strategy Play


Best for longer sessions, planning, problem-solving, and teens who enjoy depth. Dive into worlds where every decision shapes the outcome.


- Weekend game marathons

- Teen game club meetups

- Quiet focus time




















## Need a recommendation for a specific age group?


Tell NextGen Tabletops who will be playing, how much time you have, and the kind of fun you want.

Ask for guidance

# Privacy Policy



Last Updated:  7/6/2026



NextGen Tabletops ("Company", "we", "our") is committed to protecting your privacy. This privacy policy explains how we collect, use and protect your information when you use our website [business_website] ("Service").


## 1. Information Collection


We may collect the following types of information:


- Personal Information: Name, email address, phone number and address

- Technical Information: IP address, browser type, operating system and website usage data

- Cookies: Information stored on your computer to improve user experience




## 2. Use of Information


We use the collected information for the following purposes:


- Providing requested services

- Improving service and user experience

- Contacting you regarding our services

- Compliance with legal requirements




## 3. Information Sharing


We do not sell, rent or share your personal information with third parties, except in the following cases:


- With your explicit consent

- When required by law

- To protect our rights or user safety

- With service providers who assist in operating the service (under confidentiality agreements)




## 4. User Rights


In accordance with Israeli Privacy Protection Law 1981, you have the following rights:


- Right to access personal information stored about you

- Right to correct inaccurate or incomplete information

- Right to delete personal information in certain circumstances

- Right to object to information processing for marketing purposes

- Right to file a complaint with the Data Protection Authority




## 5. Cookies


Our website uses cookies to improve user experience. You can manage cookies through your browser settings. Disabling cookies may affect website functionality.


## 6. Information Security


We implement reasonable security measures to protect your information, including encryption, firewalls and restricted access control. However, no transmission or storage method is 100% secure.


## 7. Policy Changes


We may update this privacy policy from time to time. Material changes will be posted on the website with 30 days advance notice.



## 8. Contact Information


For questions or requests regarding this privacy policy, please contact us:


- Company: NextGen Tabletops

- Email: test@test.com

- Phone: 97230000000

- Address: Test street 38, Test city, Israel



Data Protection Authority: For complaints, you may contact the Data Protection Authority at the Ministry of Justice

# Accessibility Statement



Last updated:  July 6, 2026



NextGen Tabletops is committed to making our services accessible to all users. We strive to implement the Israeli Standard (TI 5568) based on WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines.


Accessibility Level: AA (Israeli Standard TI 5568)



## 1. Accessibility Policy


We believe in equal rights and the right of every person to receive information and services independently and equally. This website was designed and built with special emphasis on accessibility for people with disabilities.


## 2. Accessibility Arrangements on the Site


- Keyboard navigation support

- Screen reader compatibility

- Appropriate color contrast

- Flexible and scalable font sizes

- Descriptive image alt text

- Hierarchical heading structure

- Clear and descriptive links

- Support for 200% zoom without content loss





### WCAG 2.1 Compliance


The website complies with WCAG 2.1 Level AA, which includes:


- Perceivable: Information is presented in ways users can perceive

- Operable: Interface components are operable

- Understandable: Information and user interface are understandable

- Robust: Content can be interpreted by a variety of technologies





## 3. Supported Assistive Technologies


- NVDA (Windows)

- JAWS (Windows)

- VoiceOver (Mac/iOS)

- TalkBack (Android)

- Dragon NaturallySpeaking

- Switch navigation




## 4. Accessibility Testing


The website has been tested using:


- Automated accessibility testing tools

- Manual testing with screen readers

- Keyboard-only navigation

- Color contrast verification

- Testing with users with disabilities




## 5. Continuous Improvements


We are continuously working to improve the accessibility of our website and update it according to technological developments and user feedback.



## 6. Contact and Feedback


If you encounter an accessibility issue on the site or need assistance, please contact us:


- Company: NextGen Tabletops

- Email: test@test.com

- Phone: 97230000000



Response time: We respond to accessibility inquiries within 3 business days and work to resolve issues within 10 business days.

- "User" - Anyone who browses or uses the site

NextGen Tabletops provides Toys & Games through the site. The services are subject to the terms detailed in this document and may change from time to time.


## 3. Terms of Use

## 4. User Obligations

## 6. Limitation of Liability


Services are provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. The Company will not be liable for indirect, consequential, or special damages arising from use of the site, except where required by law.


## 7. Copyright and Intellectual Property

## 8. Privacy


Collection and use of personal information is subject to our Privacy Policy. Use of the site constitutes agreement to the Privacy Policy as detailed separately.


## 9. Changes to Terms of Use


The Company may change these terms of use at any time. Material changes will be posted on the site with 30 days advance notice. Continued use after changes constitutes agreement to the new terms.


## 10. Service Termination


The Company may suspend or limit service at any time, including in cases of terms of use violations. In case of service termination, relevant provisions will remain in effect.


## 11. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution


These terms of use are governed by applicable laws. Any disputes will be resolved in accordance with local jurisdiction, with preference given to arbitration or mediation where possible.

# Ask for a game recommendation.


Tell NextGen Tabletops about the players, ages, time available, and the kind of tabletop fun you are looking for.


- Include age range

- Mention group size

- Share preferred game length

- Note whether the group likes strategy, creativity, teamwork, or party play








Name



Email



Phone



Message






I have read and agree to the  Terms & Conditions  |

Return Policy
and  Privacy Policy



Send request









## What to include for the best guidance









### Who is playing


Ages, number of players, and whether adults are joining.








### When it will be played


A quick weeknight round, a party, a classroom moment, or a longer weekend session.








### What kind of fun fits


Strategy, creativity, cooperation, laughter, or easy first-time play.










## Friendly guidance, not pressure.


The goal is to help families feel confident about what fits their table, not to overwhelm them with endless choices.


Recommendations focus on age fit, ease of learning, social value, and replay potential.





Thoughtful suggestions



Kid and teen focused



Parent-friendly clarity

# How to Pick the Right Game for Every Age at the Table


Published: March 15, 2024
·
6 min read






Choosing the perfect game for a family game night can feel like solving a puzzle before you even open the box. With shelves overflowing with colorful boxes, complex rulebooks, and age recommendations that sometimes miss the mark, parents often wonder: "Will my 6-year-old actually enjoy this?" or "Is this too simple for my teenager?" At NextGen Tabletops, we believe the right game doesn't just pass the time — it builds bridges between siblings, sparks curiosity in young minds, and creates memories that last far longer than any screen time session. This guide will walk you through the art of matching games to developmental stages, so your next game night is a guaranteed win for everyone at the table.


## Understanding Age Labels: More Than Just a Number


The age recommendation printed on a game box is a helpful starting point, but it's not the whole story. Manufacturers base these numbers on safety standards, average attention spans, and testing with focus groups. However, every child is unique. A 7-year-old who loves puzzles might thrive with a strategy game labeled for ages 10+, while a 10-year-old who prefers active play might bounce off a slow-building engine-builder. Think of the age label as a guardrail, not a destination. It tells you the youngest age that can safely and cognitively engage with the core mechanics, but it doesn't account for interest, patience, or sibling dynamics.


When evaluating a game, look past the number and consider the skills it requires. Does it demand reading fluency? Complex math? Abstract reasoning? A cooperative game like Outfoxed! works beautifully for 5-year-olds because it relies on visual deduction and teamwork rather than text. Meanwhile, a drafting game like Sushi Go! introduces probability and set collection in bite-sized rounds that don't overwhelm young players. By matching the skill demands to your child's current abilities — not their age — you'll unlock far more successful game nights.


## The Preschool Powerhouse (Ages 3–5): First Steps into Structured Play


For the youngest players, games are less about winning and more about discovering the joy of taking turns, following simple instructions, and celebrating small victories. At this stage, look for games with chunky components, bright colors, and rules that can be explained in under a minute. Memory matching games, color-recognition challenges, and cooperative adventures where everyone works toward a shared goal are perfect entry points.


Classics like Hoot Owl Hoot! and My First Orchard exemplify what works: no reading required, short play sessions (10–15 minutes), and a tangible, physical component that keeps little hands busy. Avoid games with small pieces that pose choking hazards, and steer clear of any mechanic that eliminates players early. Nothing crushes a preschooler's enthusiasm faster than being "out" while everyone else keeps playing. The goal here is to build confidence and associate game time with warmth and laughter.


## The Early Reader Explorer (Ages 6–8): Strategy Blossoms


As children enter elementary school, their capacity for planning, pattern recognition, and delayed gratification takes a leap forward. This is the golden window for introducing light strategy, set collection, and games with a dash of suspense. Card games shine in this age bracket — they're portable, quick to reset, and often involve just enough luck to keep the playing field level between adults and kids.


Titles like Sleeping Queens and Dragonwood blend storytelling with simple arithmetic and risk-reward decisions. Children learn to hold cards for future turns, anticipate opponents' moves, and handle the emotional rollercoaster of a lucky draw or a sudden setback. At this stage, parents should model good sportsmanship explicitly: narrate your own thought process, celebrate clever plays regardless of who makes them, and gently reinforce that losing a round doesn't mean losing the game. These lessons extend far beyond the tabletop.


## The Tween Tactician (Ages 9–12): Deepening the Challenge


Tweens crave autonomy, mastery, and social connection — and games can deliver all three in spades. This age group is ready for more complex rule sets, longer play times (45–60 minutes), and mechanics that reward repeated play. Deck-building games, tile-laying worlds, and cooperative campaigns where each player controls a unique character with special abilities all hit the sweet spot.


Consider introducing gateway hobby games like Ticket to Ride, Kingdomino, or Forbidden Island. These titles teach resource management, spatial reasoning, and tactical flexibility without requiring a 30-page rulebook. Tweens also begin to appreciate the meta-game — the banter, bluffing, and negotiation that happen around the board. A well-timed bluff in Cockroach Poker or a clever trade in Catan Junior can become the story your family retells for years. At this stage, let your tween take the lead on explaining rules to younger siblings; teaching is one of the deepest forms of learning.


## The Teen Strategist (Ages 13+): Complexity and Connection


Teenagers are ready for the full spectrum of modern board gaming. They can handle intricate rulebooks, multi-hour sessions, and games where a single decision ripples across the entire play experience. But the real magic of gaming with teens isn't the complexity — it's the connection. In an era of digital distraction, sitting face-to-face around a board creates a rare space for genuine conversation, friendly rivalry, and shared storytelling.


Games like Wingspan, Azul, and cooperative hits like Pandemic offer the depth teens crave while remaining accessible to mixed-age groups. Don't shy away from games with a social deduction element — The Resistance or Deception: Murder in Hong Kong can turn a Friday night into an unforgettable event. The key is to follow your teen's interests. If they love fantasy, dive into an adventure game. If they're competitive, embrace head-to-head dueling games. The game itself is almost secondary to the ritual of gathering, disconnecting from screens, and rediscovering the simple joy of playing together.


## Building Your Family's Game Library: A Curated Approach


You don't need a closet overflowing with boxes to have a rich game night rotation. A carefully curated shelf of 8–12 titles that span different ages, play times, and player counts will serve your family better than 50 impulse purchases. Aim for variety: one quick warm-up game, one cooperative challenge, one competitive strategy title, and one silly party game that makes everyone laugh. Rotate games seasonally, and don't be afraid to donate titles that no longer spark joy. A lean, loved collection beats a dusty archive every time.


Finally, remember that the best game is the one your family actually wants to play. Involve everyone in the selection process. Let each family member take turns choosing the evening's game, and honor those choices even if they're not your personal favorite. The habit of playing together — of gathering, laughing, and navigating wins and losses as a team — is the real treasure. The games are simply the vehicle that gets you there.

# Why Cooperative Games Build Confidence


March 20, 2025
·
6 min read






In a world where competition often takes center stage, cooperative board games offer a refreshing and meaningful alternative. For children and teenagers, these games are more than just a fun pastime—they are powerful tools for building confidence, fostering teamwork, and developing essential social skills. At NextGen Tabletops, we believe that the best games are those that bring young players together, encouraging them to communicate, strategize, and celebrate victories as a team.



## The Power of Playing Together


Unlike traditional competitive games where one winner emerges and others face defeat, cooperative games unite players around a common goal. Whether it's solving a mystery, escaping from a haunted house, or saving the world from an imaginary threat, everyone works together. This shared experience helps children understand that their contributions matter, no matter how small. When a shy child suggests a move that leads the team to success, their self-esteem gets a genuine boost. They learn that their voice is valuable and that collaboration can lead to incredible outcomes.



Cooperative play also reduces the fear of failure. In a competitive setting, losing can feel personal and discouraging. But in a cooperative game, the team wins or loses together. This creates a safe environment where children feel comfortable taking risks, experimenting with new strategies, and learning from mistakes without the sting of individual defeat. Over time, this builds resilience and a growth mindset—key ingredients for lasting confidence.



## Building Communication and Empathy


One of the most beautiful aspects of cooperative games is the way they naturally encourage communication. Players must discuss options, share information, and listen to each other's ideas to succeed. For teenagers, who are navigating complex social dynamics, this practice is invaluable. They learn to articulate their thoughts clearly, consider different perspectives, and negotiate respectfully. These are skills that extend far beyond the game table, helping them in school projects, friendships, and eventually, the workplace.



Empathy also blossoms during cooperative play. When a player is struggling or makes a mistake, the group has to decide how to respond. Do they offer encouragement? Do they brainstorm a solution together? These moments teach children to support one another rather than assign blame. They begin to see challenges from their teammates' points of view, deepening their emotional intelligence and strengthening their relationships.



## Age-Appropriate Adventures for Every Stage


At NextGen Tabletops, we carefully curate games that match the developmental needs of different age groups. For younger children, games with simple rules and colorful themes make cooperation accessible and fun. Titles that involve matching, memory, or gentle storytelling help little ones practice turn-taking and teamwork without feeling overwhelmed. As children grow, games with more complex narratives and strategic depth keep them engaged and challenged. Teenagers, in particular, thrive on games that require planning, resource management, and creative problem-solving—all while working as a cohesive unit.



Parents often tell us that cooperative games have transformed family game nights. Instead of sibling rivalry and frustration, they experience laughter, high-fives, and genuine connection. These games create a space where every family member, regardless of age or skill level, can contribute and feel valued. It's a beautiful way to strengthen family bonds while nurturing important life skills.



## Confidence That Lasts a Lifetime


The confidence built through cooperative gaming doesn't stay at the table. Children who regularly engage in collaborative play tend to be more willing to participate in group activities at school, more comfortable sharing their ideas, and more resilient when facing challenges. They understand that success isn't about being the best—it's about doing your best together. This mindset empowers them to approach new situations with curiosity and courage, knowing they have the skills to contribute and the support of those around them.



As we continue to explore the world of board games and card games for young audiences, we remain committed to highlighting experiences that spark creativity, strategy, and social interaction. Cooperative games are a cornerstone of that mission. They prove that play can be both joyful and deeply meaningful, shaping confident, compassionate individuals one game at a time.

# A Calm Parent’s Guide to Teaching New Rules


June 15, 2025
|
5 min read






Introducing a new board game to children can feel like navigating a tiny minefield of excitement and frustration. One moment everyone is eager to open the box; the next, a rule is misunderstood, a piece goes flying, and the fun evaporates. For parents, the key isn’t just knowing the rules yourself—it’s mastering the art of explaining them in a way that sparks curiosity rather than confusion.



At NextGen Tabletops, we believe that game night should be a bridge, not a battleground. The following guide draws on child development insights and real parent experiences to help you introduce new rules calmly, clearly, and with a generous dose of playfulness.


## Start With the Story, Not the Rulebook


Children are wired for narrative. Before you mention a single mechanic, frame the game as a story they get to be part of. Instead of saying, “Each player draws two cards and discards one,” try: “We’re explorers searching a jungle temple for treasure—every turn we discover something new, but we can only carry so much!” This small shift transforms abstract instructions into an adventure they are eager to join.



When the goal feels meaningful, the steps to get there become far more memorable. Let the box art, character names, and theme do the heavy lifting before you ever touch a rulebook.


## Demonstrate Before You Explain


Young players learn best by watching and doing. Set up a quick demonstration round where you talk through your own turn out loud. Show them how to move a piece, resolve a card, or tally points. Keep your demo brief—under two minutes—and avoid over-explaining edge cases that may never come up.



After your demo, invite them to take a practice turn with your guidance. Hands-on learning builds confidence far faster than listening to a list of rules. If they make a mistake, frame it as a discovery: “Oh, look what happens when we try that! Let’s see what the rules suggest.”


## Use Visual Anchors and Cheat Sheets


Many modern family games include player aids, but you can create your own simple cheat sheet tailored to your child’s age. Use symbols, colors, or a single sentence per phase. For younger children, place the cheat sheet directly in front of them so they can point to it when they’re unsure.



Visual anchors reduce the pressure to remember everything at once. They also empower children to answer their own questions, which builds autonomy and keeps the game flowing smoothly.


## Embrace the “First Game Is a Practice Game” Mindset


Announce upfront that the first round is purely for practice. This simple declaration removes the fear of losing and shifts the focus to exploration. When children know there’s no pressure to win, they relax, ask more questions, and actually absorb the rules better.



During the practice game, keep the mood light. Celebrate clever moves, laugh at unexpected outcomes, and don’t be afraid to pause and re-explain a concept. The goal is connection, not competition—at least the first time around.


## Let Them Teach Someone Else


One of the most powerful ways to solidify understanding is to let your child become the teacher. Once they’ve grasped the basics, invite them to explain the game to a sibling, a grandparent, or even a stuffed animal audience. Teaching requires them to organize their thoughts and articulate the rules clearly, which deepens their own comprehension.



This also gives you a window into what they’ve absorbed and where there might still be gaps. Listen patiently, and only jump in if they ask for help or if a critical rule is missing.


## Celebrate the Effort, Not Just the Outcome


When the game ends, resist the urge to focus solely on who won. Instead, highlight moments of good sportsmanship, creative thinking, or kindness. “I loved how you helped your sister count her points” or “That was a really clever move you made in the third round” reinforces that game night is about growth and togetherness.



Over time, this approach builds a family culture where new games are met with enthusiasm rather than anxiety. Children learn that it’s safe to be a beginner, and parents discover that teaching rules can be just as joyful as playing the game itself.

# Screen-Free Game Night Ideas for Busy Families


October 24, 2024
·
6 min read






In today's fast-paced digital world, finding quality time to connect as a family can feel like a challenge. Between school, work, and the constant pull of screens, it's easy to lose sight of the simple joy of playing together. At NextGen Tabletops, we believe that the best memories are made around the table, not around a screen. That's why we've put together this guide to screen-free game nights that even the busiest families can enjoy.



Board games and card games offer more than just entertainment. They teach valuable life skills like strategic thinking, cooperation, and graceful winning and losing. For children and teenagers, these face-to-face interactions are crucial for developing social skills and building strong family bonds. And the best part? You don't need hours of free time to make it happen.


## Why Screen-Free Time Matters


Research consistently shows that excessive screen time can impact sleep, attention spans, and social development in young people. A dedicated weekly game night provides a structured, fun alternative that everyone can look forward to. It's a chance to unplug, laugh together, and create traditions that your kids will remember for years to come.



For parents, it's also a low-pressure way to engage with your children's world. You'll learn about their problem-solving styles, their sense of humor, and how they handle challenges—all while having a genuinely good time. The curated selection at NextGen Tabletops is designed specifically with this in mind, offering age-appropriate games that spark creativity and conversation.


## Quick Games for Weeknight Fun


Not every game night needs to be an epic three-hour campaign. Some of the best family moments come from quick, engaging games that fit into a busy weekday evening. Look for titles with setup times under two minutes and playtimes of 15 to 30 minutes. These are perfect for that window between dinner and bedtime routines.



Cooperative games are especially great for mixed-age groups. Instead of competing against each other, the whole family works together toward a common goal. This reduces the stress of younger children losing to older siblings and fosters a spirit of teamwork. Many modern board games designed for kids and teens incorporate this mechanic beautifully.


## Building Your Family Game Shelf


Think of your game collection like a curated bookshelf. You want variety—some strategy, some luck, some silly, and some thoughtful. Start with two or three versatile games and add to your collection as your family's tastes evolve. Rotate which family member gets to pick the game each week to keep everyone invested and excited.



At NextGen Tabletops, we're passionate about helping families discover games that match their unique dynamic. Whether you have competitive teens who love deep strategy or younger children who thrive on imaginative play, there's a perfect game waiting for you. The key is consistency—a regular, screen-free game night, even if it's just once a month, can become the highlight of your family's week.

## Product Catalog

### Chronos
URL: https://example.com/product/chronos-3lu2qv
Price: 18.00 USD (sale, was 20.00 USD)
Availability: In stock
SKU: chronosgames
Brand: Chronos Games

## Chronos **Chronos** is a game of shard-collecting and timeline development. Players are **Time-Weavers** of the far future trying to secure temporal anomalies, historical landmarks, and ancient artifacts—all in order to acquire the most **stability points**. If you manage your timeline well enough, you might even receive a visit from an influential historical figure at some point, which of course will further increase your stability. On your turn, you may: * **(1) Collect Chrono-shards**, or * **(2) Anchor a timeline card**, or * **(3) Paradox-lock one card**. If you collect shards, you take either three different kinds of shards or two shards of the same kind. If you anchor a timeline card, you pay its cost in shards and add it to your active timeline. To paradox-lock a card—in order to make sure you get to anchor it later, or, why not, your opponents don't rewrite it—you place it in front of you face down for later anchoring; this costs you a round, but you also get a **Tachyon Core** in the form of a wild-card token, which you can use as any shard. All of the timeline cards you anchor increase your temporal influence as they give you a permanent shard bonus for later anchors; some of the cards also give you stability points. In order to win the game, you must reach **15 stability points** before your opponents do.
